chief_complaint: Advanced chronic kidney disease (stage 4) with proteinuria secondary to early‑onset type 2 diabetes, currently awaiting kidney transplantation.
history_of_present_illness: The patient was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus in early childhood (2014) and subsequently developed diabetic kidney disease. Over the past decade the renal disorder progressed from stage 1 (2014) to stage 2 (2023) and now stage 4 (September 2023) with persistent proteinuria and micro‑albuminuria. He was placed on the kidney transplant waiting list in November 2023. Recent encounters focus on transplant work‑up, medication reconciliation, and management of allergic rhinitis. No antihypertensive, renin‑angiotensin blockade, or antidiabetic agents are documented. Vital signs and key laboratory values (eGFR, A1c, blood pressure, lipids) are missing, limiting assessment of disease control.

clinical_impression: The adolescent has advanced diabetic kidney disease (CKD stage 4) with ongoing proteinuria and is awaiting kidney transplantation. Diabetes management and renoprotective therapy appear undocumented, representing a major gap in care. The patient also carries a severe allergy risk. Missing vital signs and laboratory data limit precise assessment of hypertension, glycemic control, and cardiovascular risk, but the overall picture is one of high renal and metabolic vulnerability requiring comprehensive multidisciplinary management.
